# Libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(tidymodels)
```

# EDA

Reading in the Seoul bike data. The locale needs to be changed in order to properly read in the csv.

```{r}
bikeData <- read_csv("SeoulBikeData.csv", locale = locale(encoding = "latin1"))
```

Checking for missing data, there is not any. Also the website that the data is located in states that there is not any missing values. Checking in r does no harm though.

```{r}
sapply(bikeData, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
```

After that we can look at the data itself, make sure everything looks good.

```{r}
bikeData %>% select(where(is.numeric)) %>% summary()
```

```{r}
bikeData %>% select(where(is.character)) %>% select(-Date) %>% unique()
```

Making Date a lubridate date and making certain variables factors, cleaning up the date

```{r}
bikeDataClean <- bikeData %>% mutate(Date = dmy(Date)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  # Dont like some of the names
  rename("temperature" = "temperature_c",
         "wind_speed" = "wind_speed_m_s",
         "visibility" = "visibility_10m",
         "dew_point_temperature" = "dew_point_temperature_c",
         "solar_radiation" = "solar_radiation_mj_m2",
         "rainfall" = "rainfall_mm",
         "snowfall" = "snowfall_cm")

```

Some more EDA with a function that examines a numerical variable over a group .Examining rentals over the categorical variables, holiday and functioning day see sharp decrease.

```{r}
summary_cat <- function(df, group_var, num_var) {
  df %>%
    group_by({{group_var}}) %>%
    summarize(
      n = n(),
      mean = mean({{num_var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd = sd({{num_var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      median = median({{num_var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      min = min({{num_var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      max = max({{num_var}}, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

summary_cat(bikeDataClean, seasons, rented_bike_count)
summary_cat(bikeDataClean, holiday, rented_bike_count)
summary_cat(bikeDataClean, functioning_day, rented_bike_count)
```

Making another dataset for future use (based on specifications given in assignment)

```{r}
bikeDataFinal <- bikeDataClean %>%
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) %>%
  summarize(
    # Totals for bikes and precip
    total_rented_bike_count = sum(rented_bike_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_rainfall = sum(rainfall, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_snowfall = sum(snowfall, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # Means for weather
    across(c(temperature,
        humidity_percent,
        wind_speed,
        visibility,
        dew_point_temperature,
        solar_radiation,
      ),
      ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .names = "mean_{.col}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Looking at summaries of new dataset

```{r}
summary(bikeDataFinal)
```

```{r}
summary_cat(bikeDataFinal, seasons, total_rented_bike_count)
```

## Correlation between some numerical vars

Examining some possible relationships between bike count and weather stats

```{r}
# Cor of bikes and rainfall, maybe would be strong as biking in rain may not be good
cor(bikeDataFinal$total_rented_bike_count, bikeDataFinal$total_rainfall)

# Cor of bikes and snowfall, snow is worse rain
cor(bikeDataFinal$total_rented_bike_count, bikeDataFinal$total_snowfall)

# Cor of bikes and temp, dont want to bike when it gets hot
cor(bikeDataFinal$total_rented_bike_count, bikeDataFinal$mean_temperature)

# Cor of bikes and wind, does wind affect biking
cor(bikeDataFinal$total_rented_bike_count, bikeDataFinal$mean_wind_speed)

# Cor of bikes and solar radiation, bike more on a sunny day
cor(bikeDataFinal$total_rented_bike_count, bikeDataFinal$mean_solar_radiation)
```

A correlation matrix

```{r}
cor(bikeDataFinal %>% select(where(is.numeric)), use = "complete.obs")
```


# Splitting for MLR, and a bit more data handling


```{r}
set.seed(7530)
bike_split <- rsample::initial_split(bikeDataFinal, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)
bike_train <- training(bike_split)
bike_test <- testing(bike_split)
```

Adding weekday and standardizations

```{r}
num_vars <- c(
  "total_rainfall",
  "total_snowfall",
  "mean_temperature",
  "mean_humidity_percent",
  "mean_wind_speed",
  "mean_visibility",
  "mean_dew_point_temperature",
  "mean_solar_radiation"
)

# Couldnt find a way to use scale for test
# Just using apply
mean_train <- sapply(bike_train[num_vars], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
sd_train <- sapply(bike_train[num_vars], sd, na.rm = TRUE)

# Could drop older unstandardize vars
stand_train <- function(df, mean, sd, vars) {
  df %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        all_of(vars),
        function(x) (x - mean[cur_column()]) / sd[cur_column()],
        .names = "standardized_{.col}"
      )
    )
}

bike_train_stan <- bike_train %>%
  mutate(weekday = factor(wday(date))) %>%
  stand_train(mean_train, sd_train, num_vars)

bike_test_stan <- bike_test %>%
  mutate(weekday = factor(wday(date))) %>%
  stand_train(mean_train, sd_train, num_vars)
```

The models

```{r}
# these names are kinda long...
std_names <- bike_train_stan %>%
  select(starts_with("standardized_")) %>%
  names()

common_vars <- c("seasons", "holiday", "weekday", std_names)

model1 <- lm(
  reformulate(common_vars,
              response = "total_rented_bike_count"),
  data = bike_train_stan
)

model2 <- lm(
  reformulate(
    c(
      common_vars,
      "seasons:holiday",
      "seasons:standardized_mean_temperature",
      "standardized_mean_temperature:standardized_total_rainfall"
    ),
    response = "total_rented_bike_count"
  ),
  data = bike_train_stan
)

model3 <- lm(
  reformulate(
    c(
      common_vars,
      "seasons:holiday",
      "seasons:standardized_mean_temperature",
      "standardized_mean_temperature:standardized_total_rainfall",
      "I(standardized_mean_temperature^2)",
      "I(standardized_mean_humidity_percent^2)"
    ),
    response = "total_rented_bike_count"
  ),
  data = bike_train_stan
)
```

Test set RMSE

```{r}
rmse_vec(bike_test_stan$total_rented_bike_count, predict(model1, newdata = bike_test_stan))
rmse_vec(bike_test_stan$total_rented_bike_count, predict(model2, newdata = bike_test_stan))
rmse_vec(bike_test_stan$total_rented_bike_count, predict(model3, newdata = bike_test_stan))
```

Final Model is model2 (lowest rmse)

```{r}
coef(model2)

```
